I'll lay out my plan for this year, crop by crop, then put it together.

---

**My situation this year**

I've been working these 12 mu for most of my life, so I know every corner. With just the two of us at home now — my wife and me, the kids are grown and working in the city — labor is my biggest worry, not knowledge. I'll have to hire help at the tight moments: wheat harvest into maize planting in June, and cotton picking in the fall. Chili is the most demanding but brings in real cash, so I keep a small plot.

My field layout: about **8 mu in wheat-maize double crop** (the workhorse), **3 mu cotton** on the sandier field to the west, and **1 mu chili** close to the house where I can watch it and irrigate easily.

**Wheat (8 mu, already in the ground since last October)**

I planted Jimai-22 around October 10 last fall, base-fertilized with compound (15-15-15) plus some urea, about 8 kg N/mu at base. Now heading into spring, I'll topdress around jointing — another 10 kg N/mu as urea, bringing total N to around 18 kg/mu. That's what's worked for me for a decade on this land. I'll irrigate at greening, jointing, and grain-filling — three times unless rainfall surprises me. Targeting 480 kg/mu; I got 470 last year and conditions look similar.

**Maize (8 mu, after wheat in mid-June)**

Right after wheat combine, I'll no-till drill Zhengdan-958 directly into the stubble — the window is 5-7 days, no time to plow. Base fertilizer with the planter, about 8 kg N/mu, then topdress at V6-V8 with another 9 kg N/mu urea. One irrigation at tasseling if July is dry, maybe two. Target 520 kg/mu. I'll spray once for corn borer in late July.

**Cotton (3 mu, planted late April)**

Cotton prices have been soft but I keep it because the land suits it and I've grown it for 30 years. Plant mid-to-late April after soil warms, mulch film, about 15 kg N/mu total split between base and bloom stage. Two irrigations — one at squaring, one at peak bloom. Pest pressure is my headache — I'll scout weekly and spray 3-4 times for aphids and bollworm. Picking starts in September and stretches into October; I'll hire two people for two weeks.

**Chili (1 mu, transplanted mid-May)**

High input, high return. I'll buy transplants from the nursery rather than raising my own — cheaper in labor terms. Heavy fertilization: around 28 kg N/mu plus P and K, split into base and three topdresses through the season. Daily attention, frequent irrigation (6-8 times through summer), and regular fungicide/insecticide rotation. My wife and I handle harvest ourselves, picking every 5-7 days from late July through September.
